title: Normalize ACT reconstruction loss over valid action coordinates
body:
ACT masks padded actions but then averages L1 over every slot, including padding. Appending a padded suffix therefore lowers reconstruction loss while leaving KL unchanged, making the effective KL/reconstruction tradeoff depend on the amount of padding rather than kl_weight.

Sum L1 over valid timesteps and divide by the number of supervised action coordinates. Select valid operands before evaluating the loss, and return a differentiable zero for a fully padded batch. Tests run the native ACTPolicy with a fixed decoder, proving padding invariance, the exact masked loss and gradients, and a connected finite zero when all targets are padded.

Exact-head validation: all 3 native CPU regression tests pass at `298afa3a03a227906b8f81fca9decc9417c2ca9b`. Restoring the original production files at `742c753c0d4a5d87076c8f69e5628c79a8cc5488` makes the same complete suite fail on the original behavior, with no skipped tests or import failures. [Candidate and original-source logs](https://github.com/Afloat16/vggt/actions/runs/37027462867/job/110905636728).

title: Keep zero-valued predictions in ACT temporal aggregation
body:
Temporal aggregation treats an action as populated only when every component is nonzero. A valid normalized joint position can be zero, so an entire predicted action is discarded when any joint is at its normalization mean. If all contributing chunks contain a zero component, the rollout silently emits a zero vector.

Select populated predictions using the query timestamps and chunk horizon. This retains valid zero components, excludes expired and future queries, and preserves the existing exponential weighting order.

Regression tests exercise eval_bc through complete CPU rollout stubs with the native aggregation code. They cover zero-valued predictions, expired queries, and unchanged weighting for dense predictions. CUDA transfer and the simulator/policy boundaries are stubbed; the tests do not claim robot or MuJoCo execution.

Restoring the original production files at `742c753c0d4a5d87076c8f69e5628c79a8cc5488` makes the same complete suite fail on the original behavior, with no skipped tests or import failures. [Candidate and original-source logs](https://github.com/Afloat16/vggt/actions/runs/37027462867/job/110905636727).

title: Apply decoder stochastic depth to attention residuals during training
body:
TransformerDecoder uses self.drop_path for the feedforward residual, but calls the functional drop_path for attention without passing training or drop_prob. Those defaults disable stochastic depth, so attention bypasses the decoder's configured residual regularization in every mask branch.

Use the same configured DropPath module for attention and feedforward. Tests load the complete native leaf module and check all three masking paths, identity input gradients when residual drop probability is one, zero parameter gradients for dropped residuals, and unchanged evaluation behavior.

title: Bound replay memory datasets by the available task samples
body:
TruncatedSequenceDataset reports n_memories samples even when a task contains fewer sequences. ER and AGEM concatenate these wrappers into replay memories, so a small task can expose invalid indices and crash a replay data loader on a subsequent task.

Treat the configured memory size as an upper bound and cap it at the underlying dataset length. Reject negative memory budgets at construction. Tests iterate a native DataLoader over a task shorter than its budget, preserve ordinary truncation, and cover empty tasks, zero budgets, and negative input.

title: Preserve infinite limits in log-space probability reductions
body:
The custom maximum-shift log_sum_exp evaluates -inf - -inf or inf - inf for an all-zero density row or an infinite term, producing NaN instead of the correct log-space limit. This also reaches log_mean_exp and Gaussian-mixture likelihoods when all component densities underflow or squared distances overflow.

Delegate the reduction to torch.logsumexp, retaining the existing shape and finite-gradient behavior while handling these limits. Tests cover positive/negative infinity, zero-density Gaussian tails, multiple reduction axes, and large finite values with an independent probability-based gradient oracle.

title: Stop n-step Bellman returns at the first terminal transition
body:
SequenceDataset repeats final frames when a sampled n-step sequence extends beyond an episode. BCQ, CQL, and TD3-BC currently sum all rewards in that sequence even after the first done, so repeated terminal rewards are counted again and alter the Bellman target.

Use a shared discounted-return calculation that includes the first terminal reward once and excludes all later rewards. For BCQ and TD3-BC infinite-horizon mode, add the absorbing-state tail to the terminal reward using the one-step discount, rather than multiplying the entire accumulated prefix by 1/(1-gamma^n). Nonterminal n-step bootstrap discounts remain unchanged.

Tests exercise each algorithm's native batch-processing method against an explicit stopping-time sum, cover different terminal locations and discounts, preserve ordinary one-step/nonterminal returns, verify that post-terminal rewards receive no gradient, and preserve fractional discounts for integer/uint8 rewards before the final batch float conversion.

Exact-head validation: all 5 native CPU regression tests pass at `636075edf92897b4284d0b2f4ed2fff8da5a7547`. Restoring the original production files at `d309eaecc18acf4152a830a895a6984b8ac71b05` makes the same complete suite fail on the original behavior, with no skipped tests or import failures. [Candidate and original-source logs](https://github.com/Afloat16/vggt/actions/runs/37027462867/job/110905636682).

title: fix: exclude self neighbors at the full cosine similarity boundary
body:
KoLeo masks each self similarity with -1, which is also the valid cosine similarity of antipodal unit vectors. A two-vector antipodal batch can therefore choose itself as its nearest neighbor and report the epsilon distance instead of the inter-vector distance, producing a spurious large entropy penalty. Use negative infinity for the local and distributed self entries so every genuine neighbor remains eligible. Regression tests cover antipodal batches, distributed rank offsets, and the analytical Euclidean entropy value with finite gradients.

title: fix: compute multistep depth scheduler phases once per step
body:
WarmupMultiStepLR advances its shared milestone index while computing each optimizer parameter group's rate. At a milestone, different groups can receive different decay factors; repeated rate queries can advance the schedule, and a final milestone causes an out-of-range access on a subsequent group or step. Derive the phase from the number of milestones crossed by the current step instead. Tests cover parameter-group ratios across the complete training horizon, coincident milestones, repeated queries, and optimizer/scheduler checkpoint restoration.

title: fix: pass training duration to iterative depth schedulers
body:
The depth scheduler factory creates a filtered copy of constructor arguments, but writes total_iters to the original dictionary and then invokes the constructor with the unchanged copy. ConstantLR, LinearLR, and PolynomialLR therefore use PyTorch's default five iterations instead of the configured training duration. Update the dictionary actually passed to the constructor. Tests check all three scheduler durations, the analytical linear-decay trajectory, and that the caller's configuration is preserved.

title: fix: stabilize SILog metrics without hiding invalid predictions
body:
SILog currently subtracts two large log-error moments, then replaces every NaN result with zero. This loses a small but nonzero dispersion under a large multiplicative depth bias and also reports a perfect SILog score for invalid predictions or an empty evaluation mask. Compute the population variance directly with torch.var(correction=0), which centers the error before accumulation and preserves undefined results. Tests compare a large-bias example with a float64 centered-moment oracle, cover constant-scale and singleton inputs, and ensure invalid or fully masked inputs remain undefined.

title: fix: preserve homogeneous coordinates when adding grid axes
body:
xy_grid(..., homogeneous=True, unsqueeze=...) constructs three coordinate planes but then only unsqueezes the first two, dropping the homogeneous coordinate. Its NumPy path also concatenates the list returned by meshgrid with a tuple and calls Tensor.unsqueeze on arrays. Normalize the coordinate container to a tuple and add the requested axis to every plane using the corresponding backend operation. Tests compare NumPy and PyTorch grids, check each supported axis placement, and verify the complete [u,v,1] grid with a nonzero origin.

title: fix: count points instead of coordinates in unmasked cloud normalization
body:
Average point-cloud normalization obtains its denominator from invalid_to_zeros. With a spatial validity mask this is the number of points, but without a mask the helper counts scalar coordinates, yielding three times as many elements for XYZ maps. The optional-mask path therefore changes the normalization scale by a factor of three, and a pair with only one masked view combines incompatible units. Count flattened points locally for unmasked views. Tests cover mask equivalence for all average-distance modes, differently sized map pairs, mixed masked/unmasked views, and gradients against a mean-distance oracle.

title: fix: normalize masked reductions by the broadcast mask coverage
body:
reduce_mean documents broadcastable masks, but its numerator broadcasts a shared mask across channels/batches while its denominator sums only the original mask. A mask with a singleton channel axis therefore multiplies the reported mean by the channel count. Broadcast the mask before both reductions and replace excluded values before multiplication so masked NaN/Inf entries do not contaminate the result. Tests cover shared-channel masks, integer weights, excluded nonfinite values, connected zero for an empty mask, and gradients.

title: fix: exclude masked coordinates before surface-normal differentiation
body:
The surface-normal path computes cross products and normalizes every point, then masks invalid stencils afterward. A NaN or infinite point excluded by the validity mask can still introduce NaN gradients through the unused cross-product/normalization branches. Replace masked coordinates before those operations while retaining the existing stencil validity masks. Tests verify valid normals are invariant to excluded nonfinite coordinates, compare normal-loss values and gradients with finite replacements, and check finite zero gradients at masked points.

title: fix: honor optional confidence in the regression objective
body:
regression_loss documents optional confidence, but unconditionally indexes conf even when an explicit gradient-loss selector disables spatial loss. Treat missing confidence as unit confidence and only reshape a confidence map when it exists. This preserves gamma*distance for the confidence objective and keeps confidence-named gradient paths usable without a confidence map. title: fix(train): save and restore gradient scaler state in checkpoints
body:
FP16 checkpoint resume currently restores model and AdamW state but recreates GradScaler with its initial scale and growth tracker. After scale adaptation this changes overflow detection and optimizer-step behavior relative to the saved training state. Save scaler.state_dict alongside optimizer state and restore it when present; legacy and disabled-scaler checkpoints remain supported.

They check saved scale/tracker state, restoration from a deliberately adapted scale/tracker, and compatibility with legacy/disabled checkpoints. CPU float32 model arithmetic exercises the real scale/backward/unscale/step/update sequence; CUDA FP16 training itself is not measured.

title: fix(model): accept strided next-token targets in cross entropy
body:
A standard teacher-forcing split, inputs=tokens[:, :-1] and targets=tokens[:, 1:], produces non-contiguous target tensors for batched sequences. GPT.forward currently flattens targets with view and raises RuntimeError for this input. Use reshape when flattening logits and targets so contiguous inputs retain their fast path and strided targets work correctly.

Regression tests run the complete native GPT, compare losses with an independent logsumexp/selected-token oracle (including ignore_index masks), and compare all parameter gradients with the contiguous-target reference.

title: fix: register frozen latent scalar codebooks as module state
body:

title: fix: encode and decode current latent scalar codebooks
body:

title: fix: use the differentiable collective result for LFQ batch entropy

title: fix: average continuous batch losses over feature dimensions

title: fix: sum exit-weighted loop losses before token averaging
body:
Loop exit probabilities already form a stick-breaking distribution whose mass sums to one. Averaging the probability-weighted cross entropy over both tokens and loops introduces an additional 1/loop_count factor, changing the language objective's scale with recurrent depth. title: fix: use positive negative-log-likelihood weights for MDLM training
body:
The default linear and cosine schedules decrease with time, so the existing derivative-based coefficient is negative. That coefficient multiplies PyTorch cross entropy, reversing the generator objective. Negate the coefficient to make the negative-log-likelihood weights positive while preserving their existing magnitudes and the mask schedule. Tests check both schedules against analytical derivatives and exercise a native masked-generator forward/backward pass. title: fix: concatenate Gaussian rollout predictions along time
body:

title: fix: weight XL chunk losses by valid target counts

title: Decode complete UTF-8 image names in binary COLMAP models
body:
The binary training loader decodes image names one byte at a time. A multi-byte UTF-8 filename therefore raises `UnicodeDecodeError` before camera loading, as reported in #407. The utility model reader shares this defect, and its writer packs each Unicode character with a one-byte format.

Collect the null-terminated name bytes before decoding and write the complete encoded UTF-8 payload. Apply the same contract to the training loader and utility model I/O.

Regression tests use an independently encoded binary fixture, verify exact writer bytes, cover both readers, and preserve ASCII multi-record compatibility. Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_gaussian_colmap_utf8.py -v`.

Fixes #407.

title: Reject degenerate depth calibration and use valid correspondences
body:
Depth-scale calibration can divide by zero for a constant monocular depth map, and invalid COLMAP depths can enter the range test. It also maps both coordinate axes using the height ratio, which samples the wrong pixels when width and height ratios differ.

Use the image metadata passed to the function, project finite positive depths, map x/y with their respective ratios, and fit only valid correspondences. Leave calibration disabled with finite zero parameters when the monocular dispersion is zero.

Regression tests recover a known affine depth relation from independently sized axes, verify the constant-map fallback, and exclude zero/negative/NaN/infinite COLMAP depths. Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_gaussian_depth_calibration.py -v`.

title: Handle UTF-8 image names in binary COLMAP models
body:
Binary image-name serialization currently treats a UTF-8 byte as a complete character, and the writer packs each Unicode character with the one-byte `c` format. Names such as `场景/été.jpg` fail to read or write.

Collect the complete null-terminated byte string before decoding, and write the complete UTF-8 payload followed by its terminator. The binary record layout and ASCII behavior stay compatible.

Regression tests use an independently encoded binary fixture, verify the exact bytes written, and cover ASCII multi-record roundtrips. Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_hloc_binary_utf8.py -v`.

title: Bound retrieval top-k by the database size
body:
Requesting more matches than there are database images raises `selected index k out of range` in the shared score-selection routine. This can occur when a retrieval or pose-pairing configuration is reused with a small database.

Bound top-k by the number of score columns. Keep the existing masking, score thresholds, ranking, and finite-value filtering so the result contains only available eligible pairs.

title: Make log scale-shift normalization invertible
body:
`denormalize(y)` computes `exp(y * scale_log + shift_log)`, but `normalize(x)` currently computes `log(x) - shift_log / scale_log`. These are inverses only in special cases such as unit scale.

Apply the affine shift before division in log space: `(log(x) - shift_log) / scale_log`.

Regression tests compare against the log-affine definition, verify scalar and per-channel roundtrips, and check that the inverse chain has identity gradient. Run `LIDRA_SKIP_INIT=1 python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_sam3d_log_normalization.py -v`.

title: Broadcast scene transforms in object batch order
body:
Object poses are flattened from `(B, K, C)` in scene-major order, but the post-composed scene matrices use `repeat(K, 1, 1)`, which tiles scenes in a different order. For multiple scenes and multiple objects, some objects receive another scene's normalization transform.

Repeat each scene matrix consecutively for its K objects before composition. Preserve the existing output shapes and decomposition.

CPU regression tests compare scales and translations with analytic scene-wise affine transforms, cover isotropic object scales, and verify the single-scene/single-object cases. title: Preserve the final batch in balanced resumable sampling
body:
`BalancedResumableSampler` only visits complete global batches. After the parent sampler has already padded or truncated for distributed divisibility, a final partial batch is silently discarded; small datasets can yield no indices even though `len(sampler)` is positive.

Visit the final distributed batch as well. Its size remains divisible by world size, so the existing equal-size load balancing preserves equal per-rank sample counts. `drop_last` continues to control the distributed remainder through the parent sampler.

Regression tests check sample conservation and reported cardinality across ranks, small datasets, distributed `drop_last`, and resume offsets through the tail. Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_trellis2_balanced_tail.py -v`.

title: Read binary mesh properties using the PLY header
body:
The binary mesh reader assumes each vertex contains only three little-endian float32 values. `write_ply(..., vertex_colors=...)` appends RGB/RGBA bytes, so reading that file misaligns subsequent vertices and face records. Header-declared float64 coordinates, reordered properties and big-endian data are also decoded incorrectly.

Use the existing `plyfile` dependency to interpret the header and select coordinates and face indices by property name. Preserve float32 vertices and int32 triangle/quad arrays, including empty face arrays. Preserve the previous binary n-gon rejection and ASCII n-gon skipping behavior.

Regression tests roundtrip the repository's colored writer and read independently constructed files with extra properties, float64 coordinates and both byte orders, and verify the existing binary/ASCII n-gon policy. Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_trellis2_mesh_ply_layout.py -v`.

title: Preserve finite gradients when Smooth L1 beta is zero
body:
With `beta=0`, the current `torch.where` computes the quadratic branch with a zero denominator even though the forward result selects L1. Backward can then produce NaN gradients, including for exact predictions.

Use PyTorch's native Smooth L1 implementation, which defines the zero-beta L1 limit while preserving the existing positive-beta mean reduction.

Regression tests check zero-beta values and gradients (including all exact matches), and compare positive-beta values/gradients with an explicit piecewise oracle. Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_trellis2_smooth_l1_zero.py -v`.

title: Read voxel PLY attribute channels without prefix collisions
body:
Voxel PLY channel grouping uses `startswith(name + '_')`. When valid attribute names share a prefix, such as `color` and `color_extra`, channels from both attributes are counted together and the reader attempts to access nonexistent properties.

Split each property at its final numeric suffix and group by the exact attribute name. Reconstruct channels in numeric order and report non-contiguous layouts explicitly.

Regression tests roundtrip shared-prefix and underscore-containing names, preserve two-digit channel order, and reject a missing channel layout. Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_trellis2_voxel_ply_attributes.py -v`.

title: fix: preserve Gym termination and truncation semantics in FromGym
body:
FromGym currently treats legacy Gym time-limit truncations as terminal transitions. That prevents value bootstrapping at a time limit. It also assumes the four-value step and observation-only reset protocols, and forwards the wrapper's reset key to Dict action environments.

Support both legacy and modern reset/step results, set is_last from termination or truncation, and set is_terminal from true termination while preserving the existing info override. Remove the wrapper reset key before reconstructing Dict actions. Tests cover both protocols and their terminal flags, legacy TimeLimit.truncated, and Dict action forwarding.

The earlier broad Gym compatibility proposal #161 was closed without merging. This change preserves legacy support and includes the time-limit, info-override, and Dict-action fixes with focused regression coverage.

body:

title: fix: reseed memory-efficient weighted samplers when changing epochs
body:
The memory-efficient weighted samplers consume private random-generator and traversal state, but inherit DistributedSampler.set_epoch without resetting that state. Reset the relevant generators, per-dataset permutations, and traversal counters when setting an epoch. Tests check deterministic epoch replay after prior consumption, distinct epoch sequences, ordered restarts, and disjoint rank index pools.

title: fix: correct flow velocity conversion to noise prediction
body:
For a flow trajectory x_sigma = (1 - sigma) * x0 + sigma * epsilon with velocity v = epsilon - x0, noise prediction is epsilon = x_sigma + (1 - sigma) * v. The optional noise-prediction branches in the DPM and UniPC schedulers currently subtract that velocity term and return the wrong endpoint.

Correct the conversion sign in both schedulers. Native tests independently construct data/noise endpoints across sigma in [0, 1], check the default data-prediction branch, and verify sample/velocity gradients. Coverage concerns the conversion boundary; it does not claim an end-to-end trajectory for the optional noise-prediction solvers.
